description: Feature description collision audit on the NLA-class 16th verifier SAE. Checks whether SAE dictionary atoms are so similar that an auto-interpretability system would assign them near-identical descriptions — a known failure mode when SAEs learn redundant features instead of diverse semantic bases.

methodology_note: Collision rate is measured as fraction of (n_features choose 2) pairs of SAE decoder column-vectors with pairwise cosine similarity >= threshold. A randomly-initialised SAE with Kaiming decoder weights in high-dimensional space has near-zero collision rate by the Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma (random unit vectors in R^256 are nearly orthogonal). This is the expected baseline. A trained SAE on real model activations may show higher collision rates if the model learns to represent the same semantic concept through multiple redundant atoms.
